candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall establish and enforce specific limits to implement the provisions of 40 CFR Parts 403.5(a) and (b), as required by 40 CFR Part 403.5(c).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether limits developed under 40 CFR 403.5 are enforceable numeric discharge limits for comparison to reported measurements depends on how 'specific limits' under this pretreatment provision are identified and applied.

candidates.exact_span: Such BMPs shall be considered local limits and Pretreatment Standards.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Treating BMPs as local limits and pretreatment standards could bring additional enforceable numeric or prohibition-based limits into scope for limit-applicability and exceedance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: All specific prohibitions or limits developed under this requirement are deemed to be conditions of this permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a limit is a permit condition affects whether it is an enforceable limit for compliance comparison versus report-only or non-operative text.

candidates.exact_span: The specific prohibitions set out in 40 CFR Part 403.5(b) shall be enforced by the permittee unless modified under this provision.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Incorporation of 40 CFR 403.5(b) prohibitions, and whether they were modified locally, could change which enforceable limits apply to evaluated discharges.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall analyze the treatment facility influent and effluent for the presence of the toxic pollutants listed in 40 CFR 122 Appendix D (NPDES Application Testing Requirements) Table II at least once/year and the toxic pollutants in Table III at least once/3 months.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of which pollutants fall in Table II versus Table III, and how 'at least once/year' and 'at least once/3 months' are counted across Federal FY2025, could change which monitoring obligations were required.

candidates.exact_span: If, based upon information available to the permittee, there is reason to suspect the presence of any toxic or hazardous pollutant listed in Table V, or any other pollutant, known or suspected to adversely affect treatment plant operation, receiving water quality, or solids disposal procedures, analysis for those pollutants shall be performed at least once/3 months on both the influent and the effluent.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This conditional trigger governs when additional quarterly influent and effluent monitoring is required; interpreting 'reason to suspect' and which pollutants qualify could change required-monitoring findings and how missing results for those periods are classified.

candidates.exact_span: The influent and effluent samples collected shall be composite samples consisting of at least 12 aliquots collected at approximately equal intervals over a representative 24 hour period and composited according to flow.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sampling design requirements can affect whether reported measurements satisfy the permit's monitoring obligation and whether they are the correct basis for numeric limit comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Sampling and analytical procedures shall be in accordance with guidelines established in 40 CFR 136.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which 40 CFR Part 136 methods and procedures apply can change whether a reported value is valid for compliance comparison and whether monitoring met permit requirements.

candidates.exact_span: The effluent samples shall be analyzed to a level at least as low as required in (6) below.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The required analytical detection/quantitation level, as defined by the cross-referenced paragraph (6), affects whether a reported measurement can be compared to an enforceable numeric limit or must be treated as non-comparable or unresolved.

candidates.exact_span: Where composite samples are inappropriate, due to sampling, holding time, or analytical constraints, at least 4 grab samples, taken at equal intervals over a representative 24 hour period, shall be taken.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether composite sampling is inappropriate, and whether the grab-sample alternative was properly invoked, can change monitoring-obligation satisfaction and the validity of measurements used for limit exceedance evaluation.
